;Business and economy
*[[Argentine debt restructuring]]
**The [[Government of Argentina|government]] approves a proposed deal with the [[U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission]] (SEC) to [[Restructuring|restructure]] around [[United States dollar|$]]65 billion in foreign [[government bond]]s, following [[President of Argentina|President]] [[Alberto Fernández]]'s successful negotiations with [[creditor]]s and the [[International Monetary Fund]] the previous week after the country [[Default (finance)|defaulted]] in May. The government plans to submit the proposal to the SEC on August 17. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-argentina-debt-proposal/argentina-approves-revised-debt-offer-set-for-sec-filing-idUSKCN25C04M (Reuters)]
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
**The ''[[MSC Grandiosa]]'' disembarks from [[Genoa]], [[Italy]], on a seven-day cruise in the [[Mediterranean Sea]], the first major cruise ship to sail in the Sea in almost five months because of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53802045 (BBC News)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[MV Wakashio oil spill|MV ''Wakashio'' oil spill]]
**The [[Japan]]ese [[bulk carrier]] ''Wakashio'', which stranded on a reef in [[Mauritius]] last month, breaks in half. Approximately 1,000 tonnes of oil spilled into the [[Indian Ocean|ocean]]. Most of the oil had been pumped out before the ship broke in half in the afternoon. Around 166 tonnes of oil remained after the break, and authorities are working to remove it. Scientists call it the biggest [[environmental disaster]] ever in Mauritius. [[France]] says it will help with the cleanup. Japan's [[Ministry of the Environment (Japan)|ministry of environment]] announced that it will send officials and other specialists to look at the damage. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mauritius-environment-japan/japanese-ship-involved-in-mauritius-oil-spill-breaks-apart-idUSKCN25B09K (Reuters)]
*Two [[Lighter (barge)|lighter]] vessels capsize in the [[Bay of Bengal]], near the island of [[Bhasan Char]] in [[Bangladesh]]. The country's [[Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Authority|Inland Water Transport Authority]] report that 13 crew members from one vessel en route to the [[Narayanganj District]] from [[Chittagong]] are missing, while all 12 crew members from the other vessel were rescued. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/asia-pacific/bangladesh-13-missing-12-rescued-as-vessels-capsize/1943371 (Anadolu Agency)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark]]
****[[Prime Minister of Denmark|Prime Minister]] [[Mette Frederiksen]] mandates the [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|wearing of face masks]] on all [[Transport in Denmark|public transport]] in the country, effective August 22, in an effort to control the spread of the virus. [https://www.dailysabah.com/world/europe/denmark-makes-masks-compulsory-on-public-transport-as-covid-19-cases-rise (AFP via ''Daily Sabah'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****The daily number of new COVID-19 cases in [[France]] tops 3,000 for the first time since lockdown eased. [https://www.france24.com/en/20200815-france-reports-post-lockdown-peak-with-3-310-new-covid-19-cases-in-24-hours (France 24)] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malta]]
****[[Malta]] reports 72 new COVID-19 cases in the last 24 hours. It is the highest single increase in new cases in the country since the pandemic began. [https://timesofmalta.com/articles/view/record-number-of-new-covid-19-cases-72-test-positive.812052.amp (''Times of Malta'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland]]
****[[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] reports 200 new cases but no deaths in the last 24 hours. This is the highest number of daily cases since May. [https://www.irishtimes.com/news/ireland/irish-news/coronavirus-200-new-cases-reported-in-largest-daily-total-since-may-1.4331414 (''The Irish Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]], [[COVID-19 vaccine]]
****[[Russia]] announces the production of the first batch of its [[Gam-COVID-Vac|Sputnik V]] vaccine. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/russia-produces-first-batch-of-covid-19-vaccine-sputnik-v-report/story-4Xj57TsCDanapDJ1vhbacI.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[South Korea]] reports 166 new cases of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. From that number, 139 were traced to [[Seoul]] and [[Gyeonggi Province]] and a significant portion of them were linked to cluster infections involving [[Christianity in Korea|churchgoers]]. It is the highest number of reported new cases since March 11. [https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2020/08/6ff6f6d2d075-s-korea-reports-166-new-coronavirus-cases-biggest-rise-since-march.html (Kyodo News)]
****After a spike in new cases, the government decides to tighten [[social distancing]] measures in Seoul and surrounding areas. Many measures that are to be implemented include restricting numbers of gatherings and sports events played behind closed doors. [https://dunia.tempo.co/read/1376160/korea-selatan-perketat-social-distancing-covid-19-di-seoul (Tempo)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Ministry of State Owned Enterprises (Indonesia)|Minister of State Owned Enterprises]] and chief of the COVID-19 recovery team, [[Erick Thohir]], announces that the [[government of Indonesia|government]] would bar [[Tourism in Indonesia|foreign visitors]] until the completion of a vaccine. Indonesian scientists are testing a COVID-19 vaccine with [[Sinovac Biotech]], which Thohir says is likely to be completed next year. [https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2020/08/caf0d420850f-indonesia-to-close-doors-to-foreign-tourists-until-vaccine-found.html (Kyodo News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Algeria]]
****[[Algeria]] begins to reopen their mosques, beaches, cafes, and parks five months after their [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns|lockdown]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/algeria-reopens-mosques-beaches-month-lockdown-72394752 (ABC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa]]
****[[President of South Africa|President]] [[Cyril Ramaphosa]] announces a plan to ease nearly all restrictions on the economy from August 17, including lifting a controversial ban on the sale of [[Alcohol (drug)|alcohol]] and [[tobacco]] that had been imposed in July, as infections peak. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-53795339 (BBC News)]

;International relations
*[[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]]
***The government of the Netherlands issues a travel warning advising the public not to travel to some places, including [[Paris]], the region surrounding Marseilles, [[Brussels]], [[Ibiza]] and [[Mallorca]]. The warnings come as a response to an increase in new cases in [[Spain]], [[France]] and [[Belgium]]. [https://nltimes.nl/2020/08/15/new-travel-warnings-brussels-ibiza-madrid-paris-report (NL Times)]
*Aftermath of the [[2020 Belarusian presidential election]]
**The leaders of the [[Baltic states]], [[Estonia]], [[Latvia]] and [[Lithuania]], issue a joint statement calling on [[Belarus]] to hold a new "free and fair" [[Elections in Belarus|election]] with international observers. [https://www.rferl.org/a/baltic-states-urge-new-election-in-belarus-call-for-eu-sanctions/30785103.html (RFE/RL)]
*[[Poland–United States relations]]
**[[United States Secretary of State|U.S. Secretary of State]] [[Mike Pompeo]] and [[Ministry of National Defence (Poland)|Polish Defence Minister]] [[Mariusz Błaszczak]] sign an agreement in [[Warsaw]] to redeploy about 1,000 U.S. troops from [[Germany]] to [[Poland]] so as to bring the total to 5,500. The agreement also includes a potential increase to 20,000 U.S. troops if Poland is under threat. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-53792019 (BBC News)]
*[[Israel and the United Nations]]
**[[Israel]]i Foreign Minister [[Gabi Ashkenazi]] condemns the UN Security Council's decision not to extend an arms embargo on [[Iran]]. Ashkenazi argues that Iran "will lead to further Middle East instability". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-iran-un-israel/israel-condemns-u-n-decision-not-to-extend-iran-arms-embargo-idUSKCN25B0VI?il=0 (Reuters)] 
*[[Afghanistan–France relations]], [[Afghan peace process]]
**Amidst the release of "hardcore" [[Taliban]] prisoners, the [[French government]] asks the [[Afghan government]] not to release those involved in the killing of French citizens. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-taliban-prisoners-france/france-asks-afghans-not-to-free-taliban-convicted-of-killing-french-citizens-idUSKCN25B0YM?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*[[George Floyd protests]]
**[[George Floyd protests in Georgia]]
***[[Antifa (United States)|Antifa]] militants, [[far-right]] groups, and pro-Confederacy groups clash at [[Stone Mountain]], near the city of [[Stone Mountain, Georgia]]. [https://www.thedailybeast.com/far-right-militia-pro-confederacy-groups-anti-facists-face-off-in-tense-stone-mountain-protest (''The Daily Beast'')]
**[[George Floyd protests in Michigan]]
***Members of the right-wing group  [[Proud Boys]] clash with counter-protesters in [[Kalamazoo, Michigan]], with police carrying out nine arrests, including a local newspaper reporter. [https://apnews.com/bbe825fffe22fd360dedd3ac7b220869 (AP)]
*[[2020 Thai protests]]
**Student activist Parit Chiwarak is released on bail after being arrested on Friday for co-organising a rally in July. He was charged with violating the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand|COVID-19 measures]] and breaching internal security. Protests have been taking place in [[Thailand]] since July against the [[Government of Thailand|government]]. Parit Chiwarak has said he will continue to protest against the government and for reforms in the [[Monarchy of Thailand|Thai monarchy]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-thailand-protests-idUSKCN25B0FI (Reuters)]
*[[List of monarchs of Thailand|Thai King]] [[Vajiralongkorn]] commutes the [[capital punishment in Thailand|death sentence]] of two [[Myanmar|Burmese]] nationals convicted of the [[rape]] and [[murder]] of two [[British people|British]] backpackers in 2014 in [[Ko Tao]]. The royal decree was issued to commemorate the birthday of the King, on July 28, to "illustrate the king's clemency". The pair now serve [[life in prison]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-53771925 (BBC News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Belarusian protests]]
**[[President of Belarus|President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]] issues an appeal to [[Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] as he considers the protests "not a threat to just Belarus anymore". Statements by both sides contained a pointed reference to the [[Union State]] between the two countries. Meanwhile, opposition candidate leader [[Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya]], who is exiled in [[Lithuania]], calls for more protests. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-belarus-election/belarus-leader-appeals-to-russia-as-pressure-to-quit-grows-idUSKCN25B0E0?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Sports
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports]], [[2019–20 Chinese Basketball Association season]]
**In [[basketball]], the [[Guangdong Southern Tigers]] win their 10th [[Chinese Basketball Association|CBA]] championship, bringing an end to the [[2019–20 Chinese Basketball Association season|2019–20 CBA season]], which was paused due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic. [https://www.scmp.com/sport/china/article/3097549/cba-guangdong-southern-tigers-retain-title-end-covid-19-season (''South China Morning Post'')]
